page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on x86_64 architecture featuring a 32-core Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.7 GHz. It delivers 64 dedicated virtual CPUs with hyper-threading enabled alongside 128 GB of RAM, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cache provisions include 48 KB L1d cache per core, 1 MB L2 cache per core, and a 48 MB shared L3 cache. Advanced instruction set extensions include AVX-512 with AVX512_VNNI, AES, VAES, SHA-NI, BMI2, FMA, and CLWB.

The instance provides no local NVMe storage and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying on external network-attached storage and assigned IP routing. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 32 Gbps. Synthetic benchmarks show strong multi-threaded execution capabilities, including a multi-core stress-ng score of 62125.29, a PassMark CPU score of 55792.37, and a PassMark encryption score of 51982.03, placing multi-core scaling in the top 25 percent of tested instances. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 294.35 GB/sec. Single-core metrics remain in the average tier, with single-threaded stress-ng reaching 1861.29 and single-threaded gzip compression recording 28.07 GB/sec.

PassMark memory performance registers at 2805.13 and database operation tests reach 25541.61, both in the top performance quartile, despite large-block memory read bandwidth (168.6 GB/sec) and write bandwidth (68.03 GB/sec) falling in average ranges. Small LLM inference using a 135M parameter model achieves 2455.35 prompt tokens per second, whereas a 7B model processes 105.0 prompt tokens per second. The server provides strong compute density for parallel batch execution, cryptographic acceleration, microservices, and database tasks, with reliance on remote storage serving as the main operational tradeoff.
